note: Plain numbers in a function's code that fall inside the game file's own address range, so the checker would take them for hard-coded addresses (which never count as matched source). Each is listed for one function of one game file after someone looked at the original instructions and saw a number, with the reason. The checker lets that value through as an immediate operand of that function only; memory read or written at the value is still a hard-coded address.

numbers.why: Unicode's last code point: `cmp eax, 0x10FFFF` twice in the function that writes a character as UTF-16, beside 0xFFFF, 0xD800 and 0xDFFF.

The first value past what four UTF-8 bytes can hold: `cmp ecx, 0x200000` in the function that writes a character as UTF-8, after the same test against 0x80, 0x800 and 0x10000. (The address 0x00200000 happens to be a function's start.)
